template.name: GlobalClock
template.declaration:
/* * GlobalClock — the single real-valued clock in the entire NTA (variable c). * Role: converts continuous dense time into a discrete sequence of tick! broadcasts, exactly 1 time unit apart (Assumption 1: 1 time unit = 0.1 s). * Every other template reacts only to tick? and to bounded integer counters derived from it — this is the ONLY clock in the whole model, so the DBM/zone dimension stays * at 1 regardless of how many processes are composed, which is what keeps verification tractable given the number of moving-row instances. * Also fires timeOut! the instant globalTick reaches currentLevelTimeLimit, then resets both the clock and the tick counter for the next attempt. */
clock c;

location.name: Running
location.label: c <= TICK_PERIOD

GlobalClock — the only timed automaton in the model that owns a real-valued clock (c).
Role: converts continuous time into a discrete sequence of tick! broadcasts, emitted every TICK_PERIOD time units (Assumption 1: 1 time unit = 0.1 s). All other templates evolve exclusively in response to tick? events and bounded integer counters derived from them.
Using a single clock for the entire TA keeps the timed state space compact, since the number of clock dimensions remains constant regardless of how many template instances are composed.
When globalTick reaches currentLevelTimeLimit, the template broadcasts timeOut!, resets both c and globalTick, and starts timing the next attempt.

location.name: Start
location.label: dummyExpRate

GameManager — controls the global game state, including lives, score, level progress, and Frogger's respawn cycle.
Role: reacts to game events generated by other templates. Upon reachBay?, it awards the corresponding score and, if all home bays become occupied, starts a new level. Upon loseOneLife? or timeOut?, it decrements a life and starts the respawn sequence.
frogMoveTimer enforces the mandatory 2-second waiting period before Frogger may move again after the start of the game, a death, or reaching a home bay (20 time units at 0.1 s/unit). While in WaitingRespawn, it counts tick? events until the delay expires, then broadcasts frogInitPosition! to resume play.
WaitingRespawn is intentionally not committed, since real time must elapse during the respawn delay, whereas the remaining transitions represent immediate game-management actions.

template.name: RowRoad

location.name: Running
location.label: dummyExpRate

RowRoad — parameterised template instantiated once for each moving row (vehicles, logs and turtles). Parameter id identifies the corresponding entry in the immutable rowInfo[] table.
Role: on every tick?, updateRow(id) checks whether the movement period of the row has elapsed (globalTick % speed == 0). When due, moveRow(id) shifts every object in the row by one cell, wrapping positions modulo TOTAL_LOOP (WIDTH + BORDER_DELAY) to model the required two-cell off-screen traversal before re-entering the map.
For floating-object rows, Frogger is carried together with the object whenever he is standing on it. Road rows update only the vehicles, since they cannot carry Frogger.
Following the project specification, moving objects are never reset after the game starts. Their positions evolve continuously, even when Frogger respawns or the level timer is reset. The template therefore consists of a single Running location that persists throughout the entire game.

location.name: AboveWater
location.label: dummyExpRate

DivingTurtle — single shared process controlling the global isSubmerged flag used by both diving-turtle groups (rows 7 and 10). Only one instance is required, since none of the required properties distinguish between the two groups submerging independently.
Role: abstracts the original four-state diving cycle (Emerged → Diving → Submerged → Emerging; 10/5/10/10 time units) into two observable states:
• AboveWater: Frogger may safely stand on diving turtles (combining Emerged and Diving, total duration = 25 time units).
• Submerged: Frogger dies if riding a diving turtle (combining Submerged and Emerging, total duration = 15 time units).
This abstraction preserves all behaviours relevant to collision detection, because the rest of the model only observes whether diving turtles are safe or unsafe, not the intermediate animation phases.
timer counts elapsed ticks in the current observable state and is reset whenever the process switches between AboveWater and Submerged.

template.name: TruckRow
Frogger

location.name: Respawning
location.label: dummyExpRate

- Role & Core Behavior: The Frog template models the player-controlled entity, focusing specifically on managing player movement coordinates (frog_x, frog_y) and collision handling rather than scores or lives. - States & Workflow: The template comprises three core locations: 1. Respawning: The initial state where the frog waits for a 2-second delay after respawning. Once frogInitPosition is broadcasted, the frog transitions to the Playing state. 2. Playing: The active state where the player may move, stay immobile, or wait between moves. A local clock/variable enforces non-Zeno behavior, ensuring the frog waits at least 1 time unit between two consecutive moves. If an immobile frog is hit by an object, loseOneLife is broadcasted and the frog transitions back to Respawning. 3. EvaluateSafety: A committed location reached immediately when the player triggers a movement via moveFrog(). Because it is committed, zero time elapses before safety verification occurs. - Evaluation & Transitions from EvaluateSafety: - checkCollision() evaluates road collisions, river drowning/platform checks, and home bay occupation/success. - If a collision occurs, a bay is successfully filled, or the game wins/resets via bay completion, the frog transitions back to the Respawning state. - If no major/terminating event happens, the frog returns to the Playing state.
